boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 15:1 opens with the strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.15.1), immediately followed by the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.15.2) at 15:2, which puts the riddle about the useless vine-wood in the standard oracle-onset frame. Close side: the row's final verse, MT 15:8, ends the applied sentence against Jerusalem's inhabitants and carries the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature at its own end, matched by a pe mark recorded on 15:8 in the single-witness paragraph layer. A samekh mark sits earlier, on 15:5 (sweep: 8 verses), where the riddle's own question -- whether the vine-wood, even charred, is fit for any use -- reaches its rhetorical dead end before the messenger formula כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.15.6) opens the application at 15:6. That mid-chapter mark is weighed and not adopted as the row seam: the application (15:6-8) answers the riddle (15:1-5) rather than opening an independent formula-bounded unit of its own, and a three-verse application row would not itself carry a fresh word-event onset. The row is therefore kept as the whole chapter, with the internal mark disclosed rather than acted on.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.16.1) at 16:1, the address בֶּן אָדָ֕ם (oshb:Ezek.16.2) at 16:2, and the messenger formula naming the addressee, כֹּה אָמַ֨ר אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ לִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.16.3) at 16:3, together open the foundling allegory and fix Jerusalem as the figure's referent from the first clause; the pe recorded at MT 15:8 (single witness) closes the unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: MT 16:14 is this row's last verse, and its own final words are the utterance formula נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.14), closing the first movement (the abandoned infant clothed, fed and enthroned) before the narrative turns to her unfaithfulness at 16:15. No parashah mark falls between 16:1 and 16:14 (sweep: 14 verses), so the utterance-formula close is the only mark-independent boundary evidence available for this stretch, and it is taken as such. MT 16:13 (oshb:Ezek.16.13) carries a doubled Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv forms ששי and אכלתי in place of the pointed readings; the Qere layer gives (Qere for both) שֵׁ֤שׁ (fine linen) and אָכָ֑לְתְּ (you ate) respectively. Neither Qere is used to argue this boundary; both are disclosed because the span covers them.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:51 opens with no formula device, וְשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן כַּחֲצִ֥י חַטֹּאתַ֖יִךְ לֹ֣א חָטָ֑אָה וַתַּרְבִּ֤י אֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ מֵהֵ֔נָּה וַתְּצַדְּקִי֙ אֶת אחותך בְּכָל תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עשיתי (oshb:Ezek.16.51), continuing the comparative indictment by default: 'and Samaria did not commit half your sins.' Close side: the row ends at 16:58, the whole verse אֶת זִמָּתֵ֥ךְ וְאֶת תּוֹעֲבוֹתַ֖יִךְ אַ֣תְּ נְשָׂאתִ֑ים נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.58) ('you bear the penalty of your lewdness and your abominations, declares YHWH'), a verse-final variant close matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. MT 16:51 reads (oshb:Ezek.16.51) the ketivs אחותך and עשיתי, with the Qere layer giving אֲחוֹתַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere) and עָשִֽׂית (oshb:Ezek.16.51, Qere). MT 16:53 carries three notes (oshb:Ezek.16.53) on one verse -- the densest K/Q verse in this span -- reading the ketivs שבית (twice, once before 'Sodom' and once before 'Samaria') and ושבית, against the Qere readings שְׁב֤וּת, שְׁב֥וּת and וּשְׁב֥וּת (all Qere forms of 'fortunes/captivity'). An editorial note also falls at 16:54 inside this span, disclosed as a single-witness vowel-reading divergence, not a text-critical claim about the row's content.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 16:59 opens with the messenger formula כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.16.59) ('for thus says the Lord YHWH'), turning from the sisters comparison to YHWH's own covenant memory; the running text reads the ketiv ועשית in place of the pointed form here (oshb:Ezek.16.59). Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, MT 16:63, the whole verse לְמַ֤עַן תִּזְכְּרִי֙ וָבֹ֔שְׁתְּ וְלֹ֨א יִֽהְיֶה לָּ֥ךְ עוֹד֙ פִּתְח֣וֹן פֶּ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י כְּלִמָּתֵ֑ךְ בְּכַפְּרִי לָךְ֙ לְכָל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ית נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.63), whose final words are the utterance formula, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse -- the strongest close available in the chapter, mark, refrain and chapter-end all coinciding. Inside the row, MT 16:62 closes with the second-person recognition formula, the whole verse וַהֲקִימוֹתִ֥י אֲנִ֛י אֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֖עַתְּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.62) ('and you shall know that I am YHWH'), a genuine refrain close that is nonetheless not treated as the row's own end, since 16:63 both continues the same covenant sentence grammatically and carries the stronger, mark-corroborated close.

Close side: the row runs through 18:20; its opening clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב (oshb:Ezek.18.20) ('the soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear his father's iniquity') restates 18:4's thesis and closes the argument, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: the pe recorded at MT 18:32 (single witness) closes the preceding unit before it, corroborating this row's onset from the far side of the seam; MT 19:1 itself opens with the distinct qinah-command onset וְאַתָּה֙ שָׂ֣א קִינָ֔ה אֶל נְשִׂיאֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.1) ('and you, take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel') -- not a word-event formula and not a son-of-man address, but the genre-naming command proper to a lament. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own colophon, MT 19:14, the whole verse וַתֵּצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִמַּטֵּ֤ה בַדֶּ֨יהָ֙ פִּרְיָ֣הּ אָכָ֔לָה וְלֹא הָ֥יָה בָ֛הּ מַטֵּה עֹ֖ז שֵׁ֣בֶט לִמְשׁ֑וֹל קִ֥ינָה הִ֖יא וַתְּהִ֥י לְקִינָֽה (oshb:Ezek.19.14), whose last clause names its own genre a second time ('this is a lamentation, and it is used as a lamentation'), matched by a pe recorded on this same verse. A pe also falls mid-chapter, on 19:9, at the close of the lion-cubs figure (אֲרָי֖וֹת, oshb:Ezek.19.2) -- לְמַ֗עַן לֹא יִשָּׁמַ֥ע קוֹל֛וֹ ע֖וֹד אֶל הָרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.19.9) ('so that his voice should no more be heard on the mountains of Israel') -- immediately before the second figure opens at 19:10, אִמְּךָ֥ כַגֶּ֛פֶן בְּדָמְךָ֖ עַל מַ֣יִם שְׁתוּלָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.19.10) ('your mother was like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water'). That internal mark is disclosed and weighed, not adopted as a row seam: the colophon at 19:14 names the whole composition, both figures together, a single lamentation, so the span is kept as one row rather than split at its own internal parashah break.
